Yes, intra-abdominal desmoid disease can affect patients with an ileal pouch differently than those with an ileorectal anastomosis. 

In patients with an ileal pouch, desmoid disease may cause more complications due to the pouch's location and function. The desmoid tumor can exert pressure on the pouch, leading to pouch dysfunction, obstruction, or other issues. In contrast, patients with an ileorectal anastomosis may experience fewer complications related to the desmoid disease, as the tumor is less likely to directly impact the anastomosis site.

However, the overall management and treatment of intra-abdominal desmoid disease remain similar for both patient groups, focusing on a multidisciplinary approach that may include surgery, medical therapy, and observation. The specific treatment plan depends on the individual case, taking into account the size, location, and symptoms of the desmoid tumor, as well as the patient's overall health and the type of surgical reconstruction they have undergone.
